Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as background noise may be transmitted. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2023. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Information Officer; Karen Lee, Chief Human Resources Officer; and David Wong, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the fourth quarter and full year 2023. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on eight key aspects: Overview of key financial performance highlights, Initiatives to improve operating margin, Same-facility admissions and patient day growth (YoY and QoQ), Trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue, Status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures, Impact of seasonality or external factors (e.g., flu season), Operating margin guidance for the next quarter/year, and Impact of recent acquisitions on financial performance.

Let me start with an overview of our key financial performance highlights, which really highlight the resilience and strong strategic execution across our 52-hospital platform spanning 12 states. We achieved another year of solid top-line growth, margin expansion, and careful capital allocation, even as we navigated labor inflation, supply chain challenges, and the move toward value-based care. For the full year 2023, consolidated net revenues reached $14.8 billion, up 8.2% from last year, or 6.1% on a same-facility basis after accounting for the divestiture of three underperforming Midwest facilities in the second quarter. This is our third straight year of mid-single-digit same-facility growth, beating the industry average of 4-5% seen at peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet. In the fourth quarter, net revenues hit $3.7 billion, rising 7.9% year-over-year, thanks to strong patient volumes and positive payer mix changes.

Diving into volume drivers central to our hospital operations, same-facility admissions increased 4.3% year-over-year to 285,000 for the full year, with Q4 up 5.1%. Average daily census averaged 7,850 beds, up 120 basis points in utilization. Our case mix index improved to 1.92 from 1.87, driven by more high-acuity cases like cardiac interventions and orthopedics, where elective surgeries jumped 12% as we cleared COVID backlogs. Revenue per admission grew 1.6% to $48,200, helped by better commercial payer reimbursements and proactive contract renegotiations that added about 150 basis points to our blended rates.

Payer mix is a standout: commercial and managed care now make up 52% of revenues, up from 49% in 2022, with Medicare steady at 28% and Medicaid at 16%. This helped counter Medicare Advantage challenges, where denials rose slightly to 8% of claims from 7%, but we're tackling that with improved prior authorization processes using our new AI-powered revenue cycle platform from Waystar.

On profitability, adjusted EBITDA for the year was $2.95 billion, up 12.5% to a 20.0% margin—expanding 180 basis points and matching the upper end of peers, like HCA's 20.3%. Q4 EBITDA was $785 million, up 11.8% with 21.2% margins. Operating income was $1.42 billion, and diluted EPS from continuing operations hit $8.76, up 14%. This came from tight cost controls: labor rose 6.2% from nursing wage pressures, but we cut agency spend 15% via our internal travel nurse program and gained productivity from Epic EHR implementations at eight sites.

By region, results were solid overall. Our Southeast cluster—28 hospitals in growth areas like Florida and Texas—drove 55% of revenue growth, with same-facility revenues up 9.4% on 6.2% admission increases and CMI gains from neuro and oncology. Florida gained from population trends and our new ASC joint venture with United Surgical Partners International, adding $120 million in revenue. Northeast urban sites saw softer 1.2% admission declines from flu season and academic center competition, but margins stayed at 18.5% through outpatient shifts.

Our tech efforts are paying off. Epic MyChart is live at 85% of sites, lifting patient engagement 22% and no-shows below 5%. Telehealth visits rose 35% to 1.2 million, or 15% of outpatient, aiding rural access in Appalachia. Google Cloud Healthcare AI pilots in five hospitals cut pneumonia length of stay by 0.4 days and sharpened discharge planning. Capex was $950 million, or 6.4% of revenues, for digital upgrades and 450 new beds, with 300 more planned for 2024.

This sets us up well ahead. We've lifted 2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.1-$3.25 billion, or 5-10% growth, with same-facility revenue at 5-7%. Tailwinds include a $2.5 billion tuck-in pipeline for behavioral health, ASC growth for the $50 billion outpatient shift, and ACO REACH savings of 2.5% on $800 million in lives.

Moving to our initiatives to improve operating margin, we've made real progress in our multi-year program. Our Q4 consolidated operating margin was 5.2%, up 120 basis points year-over-year from 4.0%, our best since pre-pandemic, with trailing 12-month at 4.8%—ahead of the acute care peer median of 4.1% per Kaufman Hall. We're targeting 8-10% sustainably by fiscal 2026, matching top performers like HCA's recent 12.5%.

We've built this around four pillars: supply chain optimization, labor productivity, revenue cycle excellence, and clinical throughput. Backed by $150 million in investments over 18 months, including digital tools and partners yielding 3:1 ROI.

On supply chain, supplies and drugs are 22% of expenses, up from 18% pre-COVID. We renegotiated Vizient GPO contracts for 15% cuts on implants and ortho/neuro devices, saving $28 million in Q4. Total joint costs fell 12% to $18,500, keeping MS-DRG 470/471 CMI over 1.85. Sunbelt sites saved 18% vs. 11% in Northeast due to unions. Next, blockchain with McKesson to cut stockouts 25% and obsolete inventory 30%.

Labor productivity, our biggest cost at 52% of revenue, tackled nurse turnover near 18% industry-wide. Our "Right Staffing, Right Time" AI model from Epic Healthy Planet improved ratios 8% without hurting quality—HCAHPS in 85th percentile. Labor as % of revenue dropped 450 bps to 22.6%. In Midwest rural spots, Incredible Health cut travel nurses from 15% to 7% of RNs, saving $45 million yearly. Premium pay tied to performance hit 92% retention in busy ERs.

Revenue cycle: denials were 12% entering 2023 with MA at 38% mix. Waystar AI cut initial denials to 6.2%, appeals to 4%, AR days to 42 from 51. Added 220 bps to Q4 margins, revenue per adjusted patient day up 4.5% to $2,450. We're growing high-acuity lines like cardiac caths in Southeast for 140% Medicare commercial rates, lifting CMI 2.5% to 1.92. California Prop 1 offset by Kaiser-like VBC at 105% FFS on 22% lives.

Clinical throughput: ALOS cut 0.4 days to 4.2 with Stryker Mako and da Vinci robotics—ortho down 18% to 2.9 days, adding 12,500 case days and $1,200 per case margin. Teladoc diverted 22% low-acuity ED, improving door times 25%, throughput to 2.8/hour. Southwest led with 1.1-day gains.

Integrated via command center tracking 45 KPIs across 28 hospitals and 50 outpatient sites. Q4 EBITDA margins hit 12.1%, up 300 bps YoY, 95% free cash conversion. Risks like 4.2% labor inflation and CMS site-neutral cuts hedged by 60% fixed debt, $800 million dry powder for tuck-ins in Phoenix/Dallas.

These position us for 200-300 bps annual expansion through 2026, beating sector 6.5% consensus.

Next, same-facility admissions and patient days growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter. For Q4, same-facility admissions rose 4.2% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, patient days 5.1% YoY and 2.3% QoQ—pure organic across 52 hospitals, excluding recent Southeast tuck-ins.

Admissions growth is our strongest Q4 since 2019, from elective rebound—ortho, TAVR/PCI, surgeries now 42% mix vs. 38%. Neuroscience up 12% via Joint Commission stroke centers, telestroke with Humana/United. QoQ from seasonal post-winter recovery, Epic go-lives in 22 sites boosting turnover 15% with AI discharge.

Patient days outpaced due to 0.8-day ALOS rise to 4.7, CMI +2.7% to 1.85 from Medicare (52% mix) behavioral/oncology up 8%, MA to 28%. ALOS stabilizing post-social barriers, watching readmissions.

Sunbelt (55% beds)—Florida/Texas/Arizona—admissions +6.1% YoY from migration, 20-bed expansions. Texas tort reform, BCBS bundles. Midwest/Northeast +2.9%, staffing mandates offset by float pool, 0.4-day ALOS drag.

Our "Capacity + Acuity" with $250 million FY24 capex for 1,200 beds/ORs in cardiac like HCA's 18% margins. Nuance Dragon cut ALOS 6% pilots, Palantir dashboard 10% capture from 4,500 physicians. Aetna/Cigna 4-5% hikes on quality.

Guide 3.5-5.0% admissions FY24, patient days 4.5-6.0%, stable IPPS, 3% labor moderation. $1.2B liquidity, A- rating beats Tenet/UHS.

On trends in payer mix shifts and revenue impact, payer mix drives our model amid macro/reg changes. Q4: commercial/managed 43.2%, down 210 bps YoY from 45.3%; Medicare FFS 28.5%; MA 12.1% up from 9.8%; Medicaid 11.7% from 10.4%; self-pay/other 4.5%. Government mix 52.3%, +320 bps, per AHA.

Five-year commercial erosion from 48% to 43% by rate compression, MA migration (50% Medicare lives), Medicaid post-unwind +15% volumes. Commercial $14,200/admission vs. Medicare FFS $11,800, Medicaid $9,400—34%/51% discounts CMI-adjusted.

Q4 mix shift cut net patient revenue growth 1.2% or $28M on $2.4B base, 75 bps off revenue per eq. admission to $15,340 despite 2.1% CMI to 1.68. EBITDA margin -40 bps to 18.2%, like Tenet.

Northeast 52% commercial, 285% Medicare OR rates, 28% revenue. Sunbelt Florida/Texas 62% gov/MA, +22% volumes at 82% rates. Midwest 47%.

Countered by 65% commercial renegos +4.5% rates on quality, 12 Humana/Elevance savings $15M. MA pathways -18% readmits, 2-3% bonuses on $450M. AI RCM recovered $42M underpayments, AR 42 days.

Stabilize commercial 42-44% to 2025, MA 15%, bundles 110% Medicare. Oncology 340B, transplants, telehealth OON. Variable expense/admission flat $8,900.

Shifts $50-60M annual friction, but 4-6% revenue FY24.

Regarding status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures, M&A is key for growth/portfolio optimization in consolidation, with labor shortages, MA 52%, supplies +8-10%. Multiples 8-10x vs. 12x pre-COVID.

Closed Southeast Health Partners Q1: 3 hospitals, 620 beds, 45K admits, 5 ASCs/2 ERs Carolinas/Georgia, $1.45B cash, 8.5x EBITDA. Accretive day one, $45M YTD synergies vs. $120M 2-yr: Vizient GPO 12-15% savings, Cerner to Epic clean claims 92-97%, collections +9%, CMI +0.3 to 1.85, ALOS 4.2.

#2 Southeast behind HCA, 18% Charlotte/Atlanta share, volumes +7% QoQ, 145% Medicare commercial.

Divested 8 rural Midwest hospitals, 350 beds, $180M revenue, $420M to nonprofit. <45% occupancy, -2% margins. Leverage 3.8x to 3.2x, $300M powder post-paydown, like CHS/Tenet rural prunes.

Pipeline $4-5B: Q4 close Texas Ambulatory 12 ASCs/25 ORs DFW/Houston $850M, $220M rev 18% margins, +30% ASC to 150, site-neutral $50M NOPAT, AI scheduling -22% no-shows.

Behavioral $300M West Coast psych 400 beds CA/AZ, shortages 20-30%, psych mix 8-12%, $40M telepsych/MA bundles.

90% domestic, UK watch.

Hub-spoke: 25% non-acute rev by 2026 from 18%. M&A 4-6% FY24 rev, +200bps EBITDA. $150M capex, $200M proceeds. 95% synergy capture.

On impact of seasonality or external factors like flu season, Q4 respiratory peak Nov-Feb, CDC 28M illnesses +18% YoY, 1.2% hospitalizations, vaccines 52% seniors.

Our ED volumes +14% to 2.8M across 52 hospitals, admits +12% to 285K, respiratory 22% mix from 17%. Net revenue +9.2% to $4.7B, same-facility 7.1%, ADC 18,200 +10%, CMI 1.85.

Outpatient/ASC -3% no-shows 12% holidays/weather, -50bps EBITDA to 18.4% -80bps YoY >17-19% target.

Northeast +22% ED urban/cold, +15% rev commercial 58%. Sunbelt +8% milder El Niño, Epic MyChart telehealth 15% diversion +$45M.

RSV peds +30%, COVID JN.1 +7% obs. Pfizer vaccines 1.2M doses +$28M pharmacy. RN contract +11% to 6.2%, ShiftMed AI capped OT 4.1%.

FluWatch HHS dashboard forecasted +10-15%, flexed 2,500 beds, Tamiflu stock +20%, LOS -0.3 to 4.6 +$120M EBITDA. QuidelOrtho tests 20min turnaround -8% unneeded admits.

FY25 normalize 8-10% ED, MA denials risk 100-200bps but VBC United/Humana 25% lives buffer. $150M FCF to 500 ICU Sunbelt, Acme Academy upskill.

$350M rev tailwind.

For operating margin guidance next quarter/year, Q1 guide 11.0-12.5%, admits +4-5%, outpatient 58% rev +6-7%. Labor 52-53% + from Q4 51.5% CA/NY merits 8-10%. Non-labor 28-29% Vizient 5% savings.

Southeast 13-14% commercial 55%, OR 85%. West 9-10% Medi-Cal lag, retrofits. IPPS 2.9% -2% sequester 35% Medicare.

FY25 12.0-13.5% +100-150bps FY24, 4-6% rev EBITDA 18-20%.

Drivers: Epic RCM 80% rollout -200bps denials 5.2%, AR<45, pilots +7% collections.

Labor ShiftMed/Favorite 2-3% hours/patient day, Care Logistics -15% OT vs. 6-7% inflation.

Vizient/HealthTrust $150M ortho/contrast bundles, OR std -10-12%.

VBC 25% MSSP/CJR +50bps CMI 3M 360.

Margin Resilience 2026: 15% IP to HOPD/ASC like Tenet, $250M tele/virtual nursing -LOS 4.2 +3-4% margins.

Risks No Surprises arb, cyber like Change. Diversified mix commercial 52% Medicare 35% Medicaid 13%.

Finally, impact of recent acquisitions on financial performance. Our Q3-close $1.2B Southeast Regional 5-hospital 1,200-bed Florida/Georgia + $450M Precision 15 ASC ortho/cardio/GI Southeast/Mid-Atlantic.

+15.2% Q4 rev to $2.85B, acq +8.5pts/$245M; same-hospital +6.8% admits +4.2% CMI +2.1% to 1.92.

Southeast $180M ann rev +7% >$650/admit cardio/onco. Precision $65M +12% QoQ cross-refer 15-20% site-shift.

EBITDA $425M +22% 14.9% +180bps, acq $45M +$18M syn, track $75M yr-end: $30M Vizient 8-10%, $20M back-office, $25M rev ortho to ASC 45% vs 25% margins.

CareSync Epic AR 52-42 +$35M CF. Tele trans care -2.5pts readmits 14.8% <16% peer, VBC 28% from 22%.

Southeast +9% rev MA 52% IPPS 3.8%. Bundles MS-DRG 470/471 ASC +30% HOPD.

Hub-spoke vs labor 5-7% malpractice. EPS +$0.28 Q4, FY $4.75-4.95 +12%. FY24 10-12% rev 15-16% margins like HCA ASC 200bps.

55% procedural outpatient. Multiplicative moat.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the fourth quarter was $3.7 billion, an increase of 7.9% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $3.0 billion, representing 81% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $350 million, or $2.10 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year 2024 to adjusted EBITDA of $3.1 to $3.25 billion.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our HeartCare Excellence program has shown remarkable results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including lean six sigma supply chain standardization and AI-driven staffing optimization, which have resulted in significant cost savings, improved patient flow, and enhanced staff productivity.

Next, Alex Rivera will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Tom. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets, enhance our service offerings, and diversify our revenue streams.

After that, Raj Patel will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Alex. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and mitigate the risk of data breaches. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions to improve scalability and flexibility.

Following that, Karen Lee will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

Karen Lee:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives to improve employee satisfaction, enhance training and development opportunities, and promote a culture of diversity and inclusion.

Finally, David Wong will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

David Wong:
Thank you, Karen. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy, and prevent fraud and abuse.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Mark Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Karen Lee:
Good morning, Mark. Absolutely. We're prioritizing a holistic approach to employee well-being. Key initiatives include our enhanced wellness programs offering mental health support and flexible scheduling, which have boosted satisfaction scores by 15% in pilot hospitals. We've also expanded leadership development academies, training over 2,000 nurses and physicians this year, and introduced competitive retention bonuses tied to tenure and performance, reducing turnover by 10% system-wide. Diversity efforts, like our inclusive hiring partnerships with HBCUs, have increased underrepresented staff by 8%. These are tracked via annual engagement surveys aiming for 90% participation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

David Wong:
Thanks, Jennifer. Our compliance program is enterprise-wide, with annual training for all 50,000 associates reaching 98% completion this year. We've enhanced auditing with AI tools for real-time fraud detection, cutting potential abuse incidents by 25%. On cybersecurity, post-Change Healthcare, we've layered multi-factor authentication, endpoint detection via CrowdStrike, and quarterly penetration testing, with zero major breaches. HIPAA audits scored 100%, and we're investing $50 million in 2024 for zero-trust architecture and employee phishing simulations at 95% success rate.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, David. Our acquisitions like Southeast Health and Texas Ambulatory are transformative, adding high-growth Sunbelt exposure and 30% ASC capacity. Long-term, they drive 4-6% annual revenue growth, 200 bps margin lift via $75 million synergies in GPO, RCM, and referrals. Hub-spoke model targets 25% non-acute revenue by 2026, with behavioral psych expanding to counter shortages. IRR >15%, positioning 10-12% compounded growth, outpacing peers in consolidation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Our AI diagnostics, like Google Cloud pilots and Nuance integration, analyze imaging and labs for 15% faster, 12% more accurate pneumonia/stroke IDs, reducing errors. In oncology, it's aiding pathology reviews, lifting CMI 0.2 points. Combined with telehealth, we've cut diagnostic delays 25%, improving outcomes and readmits. Rollout to 50% facilities by 2024, with clinician oversight ensuring safety.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Chen with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Robert Chen:
Given the payer mix shifts, how confident are you in sustaining revenue per admission growth?

Lisa Chen:
Hi, Robert. Very confident. Despite MA headwinds, commercial renegotiations secured 4.5% uplifts, and VBC bonuses add 2-3%. AI RCM recovers $42 million underpayments yearly, AR at 42 days. High-acuity focus keeps CMI rising, targeting $49,000 per admission in 2024, supporting 5-7% same-facility growth.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
